subject: consultation on INLA required, on a spatially structured model with mixed effects

messages.author: 3afef93b5704ceff
messages.subject: consultation on INLA required, on a spatially structured model with mixed effects
parts:
Dear group,

I am struggling to get anything out of a dataset which was tasked to analyse. I failed with glmmtmb, and i am now looking for someone to help me with INLA.

Here is the data:

140 observations, but only 69 complete cases. Microbial abundances across depth gradients along sediments from different locations.

about 75 outcomes: Abundances of DNA sequences in an environmental samples, following a count distribution (Poisson, Negative Binomial). Some of the outcomes are likely zero-inflated.

about 8 continous (centered) predictor variables. lots of NAs, and some collinearity.

7 different locations (5 left in the complete-cases data), can be fixed but more likely random effects. Locations are very far apar from each other. There is a strong imbalance in observations per location.

up to 30 different measurements in each of these locations, along a depth gradient. The distances between measurements are not necessarily constant. Could be modelled as a one-dimensional spatial structure of the outcome, the predictors and the random effects. Could also be an important predictor.

in glmmtmb i set up:
glmmTMB(outcome ~ Precictors +
                  (1|Location)+
                  ar1(Measurement Depth + 0 | Location),
                #ziformula = ~1,
                data=total, family=poisson)

but these models very often fail to converge. And if they convert, the residuals seem non-random.

So, i need a model that incorporates non-gaussian outcomes, some continous variables with NAs, an imbalanced random effect, spatial structures and (sometimes) many Zeroes of the outcome.

Any help or advice is appreciated. A cooperation can also yield a co-authorship on a future publication.
